name: The Digit Sum of an Integer
description: Construct a program that calculates the sum of the digits of an integer.

comments.content: We need variable num to store the integer that we want to sum up its digits.
We need variable lastDigit to point to the digit in the 1's position of the integer.
We need variable total to store the sum of the digits of the integer. We initialize it to 0.

To sum up the digits in the integer we could extract each digit of the integer from right to left and add that to a variable that stores the sum of the digits. We need to use a loop structure. In this program, we do this by using a do loop. The do loop is more appropriate than a while loop because a positive integer always has at least one digit which results in the body of the loop performing at least once.

We need to extract the last digit in the 1's position of the integer. For example, if the integer is 1234, we want to extract the digit 4 that is in 1's position of the integer. We do this by calculating the remainder of the division of the integer by 10.
We add the extracted digit to the variable total that stores the sum of the digits of the integer and store the result back into the variable total.

We truncate the extracted digit that we processed from the original integer by dividing the integer by 10. Note that this statement performs an integer division because both operand of the / operator are integer. Therefore, this division will remove the digit that we processed (lastDigit) and we can move on to the next digit.

Each time the body of the do loop is repeated, this statement prints to the default standard output stream the updated values of the variables that we use to find the sum of the digits in the integer. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given strings and value of the variables.

We need to check for termination conditions to avoid infinite loops. The body of the while loop should repeat as long as there are more digits left that we have not processed yet. The loop should terminate when we run out of digits to process.

We could check whether the are more digits left by checking whether the variable num, which gets updated in the body of the do loop, is greater than zero. If variable num is greater than zero, then it must have at least one digit, and in that case, the body of the do loop will be repeated again.
This statement prints the sum of the digits of the integer to the default standard output stream. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.
